Danaher plans an AI and robotics lab for iterative reagent development

The Abcam-based lab targets scaled operation in early 2027, with Automata supporting orchestration and robotics; the claimed eightfold speedup is a design goal.

Danaher ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

Starting with research reagents

Danaher announced its first planned AI-powered autonomous lab on October 7. Based at Abcam, it is expected to operate at scale in early 2027. The initial focus is affinity reagents, including antibodies and other molecular research tools that bind specific biological targets. This is a research-infrastructure announcement, not the launch of a patient-ready medicine.

A connected experimental loop

AI helps propose molecules, after which the lab builds and tests them and feeds results into the next design cycle. The workflow combines technologies from Beckman Coulter Life Sciences, Cytiva, Genedata, Integrated DNA Technologies and Molecular Devices. Automata collaborates on instrument orchestration and robotic automation, while scientists continue to make the key decisions.

Targets remain to be demonstrated

The lab is designed to move from an idea to a validated reagent up to eight times faster and increase annual reagent generation by up to tenfold, from tens to hundreds as it scales. These are forward-looking targets rather than a completed year of operating results. Each design is intended to be tested and verified so that speed does not replace scientific rigor.
